Pending tests (CSF, genetics, EEG, serology) are appropriate *confirmatory* or *exclusionary* steps—not contradictory to the diagnosis.

[EVIDENCE]  
- Gradual onset (~few months) of behavioral disinhibition (inappropriate laughter, profanity, impulsive physical contact)  
- Progressive functional impairment and worsening memory (subjective, though neuropsych testing shows *relatively preserved* memory — consistent with bvFTD’s typical sparing of episodic memory early on)  
- Subjective sense of “not being oneself” without insight into mood disturbance — reflects early loss of insight and emotional blunting  
- Neurological exam unremarkable for focal deficits, rigidity, tremor, gait imbalance — argues against Parkinsonian or cerebrovascular syndromes  
- Brain MRI unremarkable — consistent with early bvFTD where atrophy may not yet be visible on routine structural imaging  
- Neuropsychological profile shows significant executive dysfunction and language deficits with relatively preserved memory and visuospatial abilities — hallmark of frontotemporal lobe dysfunction  
- Provisional diagnosis explicitly satisfies Rascovsky et al. (2011) criteria for probable bvFTD (insidious onset, early disinhibition, early loss of insight, early emotional blunting, executive impairment, imaging not yet showing atrophy but compatible with early stage)  

[GAPS]  
- FDG-PET scan results (to confirm frontal/temporal hypometabolism — key supportive biomarker for bvFTD)  
- CSF biomarkers (Aβ42, tau, p-tau) — needed to help exclude Alzheimer’s disease, especially given subjective memory complaints  
- *C9orf72* genetic testing result — relevant for confirming hereditary FTD, though not required for clinical diagnosis  
- Caregiver interview documentation — critical for corroborating behavioral changes and loss of insight (per Rascovsky criteria, informant report is essential)  
- EEG result — to exclude non-convulsive seizures or encephalopathic patterns that could mimic behavioral dyscontrol  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD)
